I opened the saved copy in all three, and it worked well — it popped open right inside Link Home, showed the page as it was with a little "Captured when bookmarked" stamp, and made clear I was reading my preserved copy, not the live site.

Version 3 is my pick. That quiet line under the details — "Saved with page copy · Open copy" — does two things I like at once: it tells me a copy actually exists (so I trust it's there), and it gives me the way to open it, all without adding a big button competing with everything else on the card. It sits naturally with the bookmark's other details.

Version 1's button is perfectly findable, but it puts two buttons on every card and starts to feel busy once I picture a long list. Version 2 keeps the card cleanest, but tucking the saved copy inside a "•••" menu makes it a bit of a hunt — I wouldn't necessarily know the copy was even there. Version 3 lands in the middle: visible enough that I know it exists, quiet enough that it doesn't clutter.

And your core behavior is right on both counts:

- Automatically capturing a readable copy when I save is exactly what I wanted — I don't want to remember to do it myself; it should just happen at save time.
- Opening that copy inside Link Home rather than sending me to the live page is the whole point — the saved copy is my safety net for when the real page changes or disappears, so it has to be the preserved version I see, not the live one.

So: Version 3, and the underlying snapshot behavior is good.
